subject: Parcelize — sudden p99 latency & throughput falloff / stabilization plan
messages:

To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Parcelize SRE Team <sre@parcelize.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T14:23:00Z
Subject: Sudden p99 latency + throughput falloff — urgent

Evelyn —

We started seeing a sharp p99 latency spike and overall throughput drop in our Redwood-powered checkout feature at ~14:05 UTC. Error rates are still low, but tail latency is causing timeouts upstream and visible user friction. This started immediately after a rollout of our expanded prompt set (no model change on our side).

Attached is a short sample of request/response logs (parcelize_error_sample.log.txt). Can you stand up a bridge? Our users in NA are impacted.

Thanks,
James
VP Product, Parcelize

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, James Holt <james.holt@parcelize.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T14:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Sudden p99 latency + throughput falloff — urgent

On the bridge now. Quick notes from initial telemetry:
- p99 spike correlates with a sharp increase in KV cache misses on the gen-api layer starting at 14:03 UTC.
- Throughput drop is concurrent with queue pileup in the batching layer (we see longer batch formation times).
- No obvious kernel OOMs or GPU saturation right now; CPU latency on host is elevated during peak batch windows.

Hypothesis: prompt expansion triggered KV cache evaporation on hot keys which increased prefix recomputation and pushed batch durations up. Two fast mitigations to consider:
  1) Temporary per-customer prefix cache warming for Parcelize (pin hot prefixes) and a short-lived cache TTL extension.
  2) A policy-based routing to the quantized/model-fallback variant (slightly lower quality, much lower CPU overhead) for non-live-critical routes.

Can Parcelize reduce RPS for lower-priority calls? If not, we can push a routing override and TTL bump from our side. Creating INF-7214 to track.

—Ben
Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: kv-cache-evaporation-hypothesis.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, James Holt <james.holt@parcelize.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T15:02:00Z
Subject: RE: Sudden p99 latency + throughput falloff — urgent

Quick operational asks from product side:
- We can accept a temporary 10% degradation in top-level responses if it reduces interactive latency — Parcelize, can you confirm whether you want the fallback routing for the checkout route?
- If we push a server-side routing override: need sampling + canary for 5% of traffic first, then step up. Please confirm acceptance window.
- Roadmap ask: if KV-evaporation is recurring for high prompt-variance customers, we should add an adaptive prefix-cache policy tied to keys + autoscaling per-key metadata (this is a follow-on engineering/PM request, file INF-xx).

I will coordinate customer comms with Evelyn once we have a mitigation.

—Marissa
PM, Inference Platform

Subject: RE: Sudden p99 latency + throughput falloff — urgent

Heads-up on exec plan: we can implement two concrete short-term changes from runtime side:
1) Batching policy tweak (reduce max wait to lower batch formation time) — low risk, immediate rollout to staging then canary to prod (ETA 45–90m).
2) Deploy a quantized fallback model variant and a routing override to move non-critical routes — requires a brief model load and traffic migration (ETA ~2h).

I'll open a small patch and push a hotfix branch. Rollback criteria: if p95 doesn't improve within 30m or error rate increases >0.5% absolute, revert. Patch diff attached (hotfix_patch.diff.txt).

Karthik
Runtime Engineering Lead

Date: 2028-06-14T18:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Sudden p99 latency + throughput falloff — stabilization summary and next steps

James —

Thanks for your patience on the bridge. Summary and items:

What we did (timeline)
- 14:30: emergency bridge opened; initial telemetry reviewed.
- 15:00: pushed batching policy tweak to lower max-wait (canary 5% → 25% → 100%) — observed p99 improvement during canary windows.
- 16:25: deployed quantized fallback model and routing override for Parcelize checkout non-critical calls (5% canary → 20% step).
- 17:40: overall p99 returned to near baseline and throughput normalized. No elevated error rates observed.

Customer-impact mitigation offered
- We are recommending a short-term routing override for checkout non-blocking operations (still configurable). If Parcelize approves, we'll keep the override for 24 hours while we monitor.
- As a gesture for the disruption, we will offer a one-time service credit (details in HubSpot deal PCZ-5421).

Follow-ups and roadmap asks
- Engineering: build adaptive prefix-cache policy (INF-7214) and model-variant warmup improvements (INF-7215). Target: Q4 roadmap discussion.
- Product: agree on acceptable quality vs latency trade for fallback routing; write SLA note for critical routes.
- Postmortem: we will share a draft in 72 hours and a closure plan in 7 days.

Attachments: incident-intake-parcelize-20280614.docx, kv-cache-evaporation-hypothesis.pdf, hotfix_patch.diff.txt

If Parcelize is good with the 24-hour routing override, please reply here and we will formalize the change and the credit.

—Evelyn
Senior Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
